Subject: Follow-up: admin activity trail exports and immutability

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the quick demo earlier. As we kick off the security intake for Heartland Health I need to capture a few concrete deliverables we can hand to our internal audit and procurement teams:

- Confirm whether admin activity / API access logs can be exported in a machine-readable format (NDJSON/JSON) and shipped to our S3.
- Can you describe immutability options (WORM-like retention, append-only exports) and whether exported files include tamper-evidence (checksums, signed manifests)?
- What fields are included in the admin activity records (actor, ip, session id, request/response payload hashes, timestamps, model id/version, route)?
- Retention options and how deletion requests (GDPR) are handled for audit records — are audit logs ever purged as part of data deletion?
- SOC 2 scope: do audit trails fall under Redwood's current SOC 2 scope, and can we get evidence/cert status?

If you can send a short playbook and a sample export snippet we can hand to our auditors that will speed the review. Also cc'ing our info-sec mailing list.

Best,
Daniel

Heartland Health

Hi Daniel — great to meet you earlier, and thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; attaching a short playbook and a tiny sample export for auditors.

Quick answers:
- Export formats: yes — we support NDJSON and gzipped JSON line exports. Exports can be pushed to a customer S3 bucket (cross-account) or downloaded via secure link.
- Immutability: we offer export-time write-once writes to S3 and support S3 Object Lock (governance/compliance modes) for WORM-style retention. We can also provide signed manifest files (SHA256) alongside exports.
- Record fields: admin actor (internal user id), oauth client id / service principal, source IP, timestamp (ISO8601), action type, resource id, model id + version, request id, token delta, and an event digest.
- Retention / deletions: audit trails for admin actions are treated as system telemetry and are not subject to user-initiated data deletion by default; however, for regulated customers we offer a contractual retention policy and separate immutable exports for the retention period. We'll need to discuss your data retention policy to align.
- SOC 2: Redwood's infra and logging controls are included in our SOC 2; we can share the attestation under NDA or via your procurement portal.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi (cc'd) to confirm API endpoints and share a short sample export schema and an example NDJSON file.
2) Share SOC 2 attestation and specific evidence artifacts (audit-usage screenshots / export logs) — Marissa will coordinate evidence transfer.
3) Schedule a tech deep-dive to validate S3 Object Lock and cross-account upload configuration with your cloud engineers.

Attachments: redwood-admin-audit-playbook-v0.1.pdf, sample-activity-export-20261003.ndjson

Thanks — Vanessa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: admin activity trail exports and immutability (technical details)

Hi Daniel — adding the technical details you asked for so your infra team has something to evaluate quickly. Below is a concise summary of the export and log model. If you want, we can run a live export during the deep-dive.

1) Export mechanics- Export API: POST /v1/admin-logs/export with parameters (start_ts, end_ts, format=ndjson|jsonl, destination=s3|download).- S3: we support cross-account uploads via an STS role you create; files are written atomically (write-then-rename pattern) and we optionally emit a signed manifest file containing file checksums (SHA256) and a manifest signature (RSA-2048) for tamper evidence.

2) Immutability options- S3 Object Lock: supported (compliance & governance modes) — recommended for long-term retention.- Append-only exports: exports are generated as incremental NDJSON files (sequence numbers in filenames) so you can checkpoint and reconcile.

3) Record schema (fields in each event)- event_id
- event_ts (ISO8601 with ms)
- actor_type (human|service)
- actor_id (internal user id / service id)
- oauth_client_id
- ip_address
- action (e.g., model.deploy, api.invoke, config.change)
- resource_type
- resource_id
- request_id
- model_id
- model_version
- response_code
- token_delta
- payload_hash (SHA256 of request payload)

4) Querying / forensic access- We provide a read-only admin activity API and a time-range query endpoint (supports up to 90 days hot query; longer ranges need export).

5) Retention & GDPR/HIPAA considerations- By default, immutable operational audit trails are retained under our telemetry policy and are included in SOC 2 controls; they are not deleted in response to a user data deletion request unless we have a contractual agreement that specifically scopes those records. For HIPAA customers we can map identifiers and provide a retention/export approach compatible with Business Associate Agreement requirements.

6) Certifications & evidence- Our SOC 2 Type II report covers logging and access controls in the production environment. We can provide the attestation PDF and a redacted evidence pack on request (NDAs/portal).

If you can share a preferred time for the tech deep-dive, and an S3 role ARN for a test bucket, I’ll prepare a live export run and a sample manifest signed by our key.

Regards,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
